1	package factstore
2	
3	import (
4		"fmt"
5		"os"
6		"sort"
7		"strings"
8	
9		"github.com/entireio/entire-brain/factmerge"
10		"github.com/entireio/entire-brain/internal/cli/internal/base"
11		bmanifest "github.com/entireio/entire-brain/internal/cli/internal/manifest"
12	)
13	
14	// integrity.go cross-checks the manifest's declared fact source against
15	// the facts the store can actually produce — both HOW MANY it produces and
16	// WHICH ones, because a corruption can leave the first right while destroying
17	// the second (see COUNTS ARE NOT ENOUGH below).
18	//
19	// sources.facts in the manifest is a CLAIM: "this brain holds N facts". Every
20	// health surface printed that claim as though it were an observation, and
21	// nothing ever compared it to the store. A facts.ndjson that had gone lossy —
22	// a line overwritten with valid JSON that is not a fact record, a truncated
23	// file, a botched hand edit — therefore kept reporting N on `status`, `doctor`
24	// and `facts map` while recall returned fewer, `get fact:<id>` said "not
25	// found", and `search` volunteered that the answer "may genuinely not be in
26	// the brain". For a durable-memory product that last line converts silent data
27	// loss into an affirmative false statement.
28	//
29	// The history index already solves this and its wording is the model:
30	//
31	//	history index size does not match the manifest; run `entire brain refresh
32	//	history` to rebuild it
33	//
34	// Note WHERE that check lives. It is not inside the per-record reader; it is
35	// in the function that loads the artifact the manifest declares, so every
36	// caller of that artifact inherits it and the REBUILD path — which must be
37	// able to run against the damaged artifact — does not. Facts need the same
38	// shape, and Load is the wrong seam for three reasons:
39	//
40	//  1. Load is per-branch and the manifest records only a total across
41	//     branches, so Load cannot know what N is for the branch it is
42	//     reading.
43	//  2. Its ~30 callers include distill, remember, facts gc/promote/merge and
44	//     refresh — the very commands that REPAIR a lossy store. A loader that
45	//     failed closed would wedge the store shut with no way out.
46	//  3. The manifest's count is produced from the same folded read Load serves
47	//     (see updateFactSourceManifestLocked). Checking the claim with the same
48	//     view that produced it makes the check an exact inverse: any
49	//     disagreement is real.
50	//
51	// So the check lives here, beside MissingBranchStores — the existing seam
52	// for "the manifest names something the store cannot produce" — and every
53	// surface reads one report. The retrieval note inherits through the single
54	// emptyResultBlindSpot choke point, which covers recall, search, query and
55	// retrieve at once.
56	
57	// COUNTS ARE NOT ENOUGH. The first cut of this check compared Declared against
58	// Readable and nothing else, which leaves a corruption that PRESERVES the count
59	// completely invisible: overwrite one line of facts.ndjson with a copy of
60	// another and the store still yields N records, still parses, still declares N
61	// — and the fact whose line was taken is gone. `get fact:<id>` says "not
62	// found", doctor says "facts: ok", and `search` goes back to volunteering that
63	// the answer "may genuinely not be in the brain". That is the same affirmative
64	// false statement this file exists to eliminate, reached by a different route.
65	//
66	// The obvious repair — compare the declared id SET against the readable one —
67	// is not available: sources.facts records counts (facts/distilled/authored/
68	// superseded/by_kind), never ids, and putting ids there would not help. That
69	// manifest is re-derived from the store itself by SummarizeSource on every
70	// mutating remember, refresh, gc, promote and retract, so a declared id set would
71	// re-baseline onto the damage at the next write exactly as the count does, and
72	// would cry loss on every legitimate id-changing operation in between.
73	//
74	// What IS checkable from the store alone, with no bookkeeping and nothing that
75	// can go stale, is the invariant the store is written under: WITHIN ONE BRANCH
76	// AN ID IDENTIFIES EXACTLY ONE FACT. Every writer keys by id before it writes
77	// (factmerge.Upsert, factmerge.Promote via IndexOf, factmerge.GC), so a branch
78	// that yields the same id twice was not written by this program. The second
79	// record did not join the fact set; it stands where a different fact used to
80	// be. That is loss, and it is loss the count cannot see.
81	//
82	// Per BRANCH, emphatically not per brain. A fact id is sha256 of normalized
83	// text plus sorted paths (factmerge.RecordID) — the branch is not in it — so
84	// the same fact carried between branches keeps its id, which is precisely what
85	// `facts promote` does on purpose. A brain-wide id set would report data loss
86	// on every promote, and a check that cries loss on a legitimate operation is
87	// worse than the hole it closes.
88	
89	// DefectMode names WHICH way the store fails the manifest. They are
90	// different user situations and must not collapse into one sentence: "not
91	// built" is a rebuild, "corrupt" is a repair, "lossy" is data that is gone and
92	// has to be re-distilled, and "duplicated" is data that was overwritten while
93	// the numbers stayed right.
94	type DefectMode string
95	
96	const (
97		// DefectNone is a store that can produce what the manifest declares.
98		DefectNone DefectMode = ""
99		// DefectMissing: a declared branch has no facts.ndjson at all.
100		// Already detected by MissingBranchStores; kept in its own words.
101		DefectMissing DefectMode = "missing"
102		// DefectUnreadable: a line will not parse. The store is corrupt
103		// and nothing on the branch can be read, not just the bad line.
104		DefectUnreadable DefectMode = "unreadable"
105		// DefectLossy: every line parses, but the store yields fewer
106		// facts than the manifest declares. This is the readable-but-short case —
107		// the one that used to pass every health surface.
108		DefectLossy DefectMode = "lossy"
109		// DefectStale: the store yields MORE facts than the manifest
110		// declares. Not data loss — the manifest is behind — but still a declared
111		// number that was never observed, so it is reported rather than printed.
112		DefectStale DefectMode = "stale"
113		// DefectDuplicated: every line parses and the counts are not
114		// short, but one branch stores the same fact id twice. Deliberately NOT
115		// folded into "lossy": lossy is a SHORTFALL — fewer facts than claimed,
116		// repaired by re-distilling what is missing — while this is a
117		// SUBSTITUTION, where the arithmetic is intact and a specific fact was
118		// overwritten by a copy of its neighbour. Telling the two apart is the
119		// difference between "some of your memory did not survive" and "this
120		// particular record is standing in for one that is gone".
121		DefectDuplicated DefectMode = "duplicated"
122	)
123	
124	// Integrity is the cross-check result. The zero value is a healthy
125	// store, so callers may use it unconditionally.
126	type Integrity struct {
127		// Declared is sources.facts.facts — what the manifest claims.
128		Declared int `json:"declared"`
129		// Readable is how many records the store actually yields that are facts:
130		// a record carrying an id. A line that parses as JSON but has no id (the
131		// canonical corruption in this defect) is counted in Unusable, never here,
132		// because it is unaddressable by `get`, invisible to recall, and dropped
133		// by every status/scope filter.
134		Readable int `json:"readable"`
135		// Pending is sources.facts.pending_reconcile — staged candidate records
136		// the manifest deliberately declares OUTSIDE Facts (SummarizeSource
137		// books a factmerge.StatusCandidate under its own counter until the next
138		// distill reconciles it). The store yields those records, so every
139		// Readable-vs-Declared comparison must add Pending back or a brain with
140		// one staged candidate reports "the manifest is behind the store"
141		// forever, through the very refresh the warning recommends.
142		Pending int `json:"pending,omitempty"`
143		// Unusable counts records read from the store that carry no id. They are
144		// reported even when the counts happen to agree, because a manifest
145		// re-summarized from an already-damaged store would otherwise hide them.
146		Unusable int `json:"unusable,omitempty"`
147		// Distinct is how many DIFFERENT fact ids the store yields, summed across
148		// branches but counted within each one (a fact id does not include the
149		// branch, so `facts promote` legitimately stores one id on two branches —
150		// see the file header). In a store this program wrote, Distinct always
151		// equals Readable; anything less is a record that overwrote another.
152		Distinct int `json:"distinct,omitempty"`
153		// DuplicateIDs names the ids a single branch stores more than once, sorted
154		// so the report is stable. The full set is kept for JSON readers;
155		// the one-line warning names only the first few.
156		DuplicateIDs []string `json:"duplicate_ids,omitempty"`
157		// Missing names declared branches whose facts.ndjson is absent.
158		Missing []string `json:"missing_branches,omitempty"`
159		// ParseError is the first line the store could not parse, in the loader's
160		// own words ("parse facts.ndjson line 3: ...").
161		ParseError string `json:"parse_error,omitempty"`
162		// Unreadable names legacy branch stores that will not parse. The flat
163		// store has no per-branch attribution; the field survives for JSON readers
164		// and for ParseError context.
165		Unreadable []string `json:"unreadable_branches,omitempty"`
166		// Mode is the classification; empty when the store is intact.
167		Mode DefectMode `json:"mode,omitempty"`
168	}
169	
170	// OK reports a store that can produce what the manifest declares.
171	func (r Integrity) OK() bool { return r.Mode == DefectNone }
172	
173	// pendingClause names the staged-candidate share of the expected count, so a
174	// mismatch message whose arithmetic includes Pending still adds up on the page.
175	func (r Integrity) pendingClause() string {
176		if r.Pending == 0 {
177			return ""
178		}
179		return fmt.Sprintf(" (+%d staged candidate(s))", r.Pending)
180	}
181	
182	// expected is every record the manifest accounts for: published facts plus
183	// staged candidates awaiting reconciliation. It is what the store must yield
184	// for the cross-check to call it intact.
185	func (r Integrity) expected() int { return r.Declared + r.Pending }
186	
187	// Lost is how many declared facts the store cannot produce. Zero unless the
188	// store is short.
189	func (r Integrity) Lost() int {
190		if r.expected() > r.Readable {
191			return r.expected() - r.Readable
192		}
193		return 0
194	}
195	
196	// Overwritten is how many stored records lost their place to another record's
197	// id. Zero unless a branch repeated an id.
198	//
199	// Kept separate from Lost() on purpose. Lost() measures the store against the
200	// manifest's COUNT, and a substitution is invisible to that measurement by
201	// construction: the count is exactly what the corruption preserved.
202	func (r Integrity) Overwritten() int {
203		if r.Readable > r.Distinct {
204			return r.Readable - r.Distinct
205		}
206		return 0
207	}
208	
209	// factStoreDuplicateIDsShown caps how many colliding ids the single-line
210	// warning names. The complete list stays in DuplicateIDs; a warning that
211	// printed a hundred ids would push the repair off the end of the line.
212	const factStoreDuplicateIDsShown = 3
213	
214	// factStoreIDList renders at most factStoreDuplicateIDsShown ids and says how
215	// many it held back, so the line stays one line without implying the damage
216	// stopped where the list did.
217	func factStoreIDList(ids []string) string {
218		if len(ids) <= factStoreDuplicateIDsShown {
219			return strings.Join(ids, ", ")
220		}
221		return fmt.Sprintf("%s and %d more",
222			strings.Join(ids[:factStoreDuplicateIDsShown], ", "),
223			len(ids)-factStoreDuplicateIDsShown,
224		)
225	}
226	
227	// RepairHint is the repair for a store that lost content. Rebuilding the
228	// manifest alone would only re-baseline the loss, so the fact commands' own
229	// wording — refresh, then re-distill — is what gets named.
230	func RepairHint() string {
231		return "run `" + base.BrainInvocation(os.LookupEnv, "refresh") + "` and re-distill"
232	}
233	
234	// Warning renders the single caller-facing line, or "" when the store is
235	// intact. Each mode keeps its own words.
236	func (r Integrity) Warning() string {
237		switch r.Mode {
238		case DefectMissing:
239			return "the manifest declares memories but no memory store (" + RepositoryPath + ") is on disk; they cannot be recalled — run `" + base.BrainInvocation(os.LookupEnv, "refresh") + "` and re-distill"
240		case DefectUnreadable:
241			where := "memory store"
242			if len(r.Unreadable) > 0 {
243				where = "memory store for " + strings.Join(r.Unreadable, ", ")
244			}
245			return fmt.Sprintf(
246				"%s is corrupt: %s; the %d memory(ies) the manifest declares cannot be recalled — %s",
247				where, r.ParseError, r.Declared, RepairHint(),
248			)
249		case DefectLossy:
250			detail := fmt.Sprintf(
251				"memory count does not match the manifest: %d declared%s, %d readable",
252				r.Declared, r.pendingClause(), r.Readable,
253			)
254			if lost := r.Lost(); lost > 0 {
255				detail += fmt.Sprintf(" (%d lost)", lost)
256			}
257			if r.Unusable > 0 {
258				detail += fmt.Sprintf("; %d stored line(s) carry no memory id", r.Unusable)
259			}
260			// A store can be BOTH short and collided. Reporting only the shortfall
261			// would understate the damage — the overwritten fact is gone too, and
262			// it is not one of the ones the arithmetic accounted for.
263			if overwritten := r.Overwritten(); overwritten > 0 {
264				detail += fmt.Sprintf("; %d more record(s) repeat a memory id (%s)", overwritten, factStoreIDList(r.DuplicateIDs))
265			}
266			return detail + " — " + RepairHint()
267		case DefectDuplicated:
268			return fmt.Sprintf(
269				"memory ids are not unique: %d stored record(s) repeat an id the branch already holds (%s); an id identifies exactly one memory, so each repeat stands where another memory used to be and that memory can no longer be recalled; the manifest's %d were counted, not read — %s",
270				r.Overwritten(), factStoreIDList(r.DuplicateIDs), r.Declared, RepairHint(),
271			)
272		case DefectStale:
273			return fmt.Sprintf(
274				"memory count does not match the manifest: %d declared%s, %d readable; the manifest is behind the store — run `"+base.BrainInvocation(os.LookupEnv, "refresh")+"`",
275				r.Declared, r.pendingClause(), r.Readable,
276			)
277		default:
278			return ""
279		}
280	}
281	
282	// Inspect cross-checks a declared fact source against the store on
283	// disk. A nil source is a brain with no facts declared: nothing is claimed, so
284	// nothing can be lost, and the result is healthy. That is what keeps a
285	// genuinely empty brain from reporting loss.
286	//
287	// The flat store makes two of the historical modes structural: within the
288	// store an id maps to exactly one record (a JSON object key), and a key
289	// standing over a different record's body — the substitution corruption the
290	// duplicate check existed for — fails decodeV3 closed and reports here as
291	// DefectUnreadable with the repair hint.
292	func Inspect(brainDir string, source *bmanifest.FactSource) Integrity {
293		if brainDir == "" || source == nil {
294			return Integrity{}
295		}
296		report := Integrity{Declared: source.Facts, Pending: source.PendingReconcile}
297	
298		combined, err := loadCombined(brainDir)
299		if err != nil {
300			report.ParseError = err.Error()
301			report.Mode = DefectUnreadable
302			return report
303		}
304	
305		// Not built: memories are declared but neither a store nor any legacy
306		// FILE exists on disk (an empty leftover branch dir holds nothing).
307		if !combined.storePresent && combined.legacyFiles == 0 && len(combined.byID) == 0 {
308			if report.expected() > 0 {
309				report.Mode = DefectMissing
310			}
311			return report
312		}
313	
314		report.Unusable = combined.unusable
315		for _, record := range combined.byID {
316			if !IsFactRecord(record) {
317				report.Unusable++
318				continue
319			}
320			report.Distinct++
321		}
322		// Readable counts what the sources yielded; a repeat within one legacy
323		// file folded away, so it is Distinct plus the collisions. (Repeats across
324		// files — the hosted-pull mirror — are ordinary and never counted.)
325		report.Readable = report.Distinct + len(combined.collidedIDs)
326		for id := range combined.collidedIDs {
327			report.DuplicateIDs = append(report.DuplicateIDs, id)
328		}
329		sort.Strings(report.DuplicateIDs)
330	
331		switch {
332		case report.Readable < report.expected(), report.Unusable > 0:
333			// Short even counting in-file repeats: genuine loss.
334			report.Mode = DefectLossy
335		case len(combined.collidedIDs) > 0:
336			// The counts agree, yet one file stored an id twice: a record stands
337			// where another used to be and that one can no longer be recalled.
338			report.Mode = DefectDuplicated
339		case report.Distinct > report.expected():
340			report.Mode = DefectStale
341		}
342		return report
343	}
344	
345	// InspectBrain is Inspect for callers that hold only a brain
346	// directory. A manifest that will not load, or one declaring no fact source,
347	// is reported as healthy: "this brain has no facts" is not fact loss, and the
348	// manifest's own health is a separate check that owns that message.
349	func InspectBrain(brainDir string) Integrity {
350		if brainDir == "" {
351			return Integrity{}
352		}
353		manifest, err := bmanifest.Load(brainDir)
354		if err != nil || manifest == nil || manifest.Sources == nil {
355			return Integrity{}
356		}
357		return Inspect(brainDir, manifest.Sources.Facts)
358	}
359	
360	// IsFactRecord reports whether a parsed line is actually a durable fact. The
361	// id is the fact's identity — content-derived at authoring time and the only
362	// handle `get`, recall, dedup and supersede have — so a record without one is
363	// not a fact, however well-formed its JSON. The manifest producer
364	// (SummarizeSource) and this checker share this predicate so the declared
365	// number and the checked number can never disagree by definition.
366	func IsFactRecord(record factmerge.Record) bool {
367		return strings.TrimSpace(record.ID) != ""
368	}

content.text:
All gates are green. Final report:

## PR 2 caller flip — complete, not committed

**Files changed: 138** (131 modified, 4 deleted, 3 new test files; 2,781 insertions, 3,671 deletions).

### Gate results
- `gofmt -l -s .` — clean.
- `go vet ./...` — clean.
- Fast packages (`factmerge`, `factstore`, `retrieval`, `command/...`, `patterns`, `factsync`) — all `ok`.
- Full `go test -count=1 ./internal/cli/` — `ok` (243s).
- `bash scripts/test-memory-storage-compat.sh` — **passes for v0.2.0, v0.3.0, and v0.4.0** (factstore package and cli released tests, with `-race`).

### Production fixes beyond the 15 rules (each found by a test)
1. **`parkLegacyDirs` rename collision** (`repo_fact_store.go`): the park dir was keyed on `time.Now().Unix()`, so two parks in one second failed on rename. Now `os.MkdirTemp` gives each park a unique dir.
2. **Schema-1 resurrect after purge** (`repo_fact_compat.go`): the fold unioned schema-1 view entries with the live branch files, resurrecting records an old `privacy purge` had removed. The fold now treats a view as a stale snapshot of its dir's live file: entries the file no longer carries are dropped; a view with no live file still folds whole.
3. **Legacy brains read as lossy** (`integrity.go` + fold): pre-migration manifests counted one promoted/mirrored fact once per branch file; the flat fold dedupes, so every such brain warned "N lost" and read commands exited 1. `Readable` now adds cross-source repeats back.
4. **`memories storage migrate` left the manifest stale**: it now rebuilds the fact source manifest after a changed migration (repo brains only), which also deterministically closes the one-way door.
5. **Legacy outline invisible** (`facts_outline.go`): the outline moved to `facts/outline.json`, but released clients write `facts/<branch>/outline.json`. Reads now fall back to the newest legacy outline until migration parks it; writes stay flat.
6. Earlier in the flip (already reported mid-task): legacy fold refuses symlinked/non-regular `facts.ndjson`; within-file duplicate-id collision detection restored; zero-byte `store.json` treated as absent; recall surfaces the integrity warning.

### Semantic judgment calls beyond the rules
- **Explicit `--branch` on retrieval verbs** (`search`/`query`/`vsearch`/`get`/`multi-get`) filters fact records by metadata (rule 1/10); unset means the whole store, never the current git branch. Global facts are exempt — `--no-global` stays their only off switch.
- Hosted status `Synced` bool replaces `synced_branches`; one repo-wide sync per event.
- `facts outline/map/retract` lost their `--branch` flags; retract/outline JSON no longer carries `branch`.
- The "force preserves deferred branches" distill behavior is gone: a force rebuild drops distilled facts repo-wide, keeps authored and retired records, and drops deferred sessions' cache entries so they re-derive later.
- Rule 13 nuance verified against the real binaries: a released client's recall on a migrated brain warns and returns empty — but after its own post-migration half-write, its recall does read that straggler file back until the next fold parks it. The test asserts the rule before the straggler write.

### Re-established cli compat coverage (`repo_fact_released_compat_test.go`)
Five tests run real pinned v0.2–v0.4 binaries against the current build: legacy writes fold on the first current mutation; privacy purges survive migration (including schema-1 residue removal); the straggler half-write warns `memory_unsupported_version`, folds, and reports `StragglerFiles`; hosted sync works across the upgrade boundary in three phases with failure/retry on both sides; distill/outline/review artifacts are shared both directions pre-migration and one-way after.

### Deferred
Nothing. All known failures were fixed; no rule proved wrong against reality (rule 13 needed only the ordering nuance above). Per instructions, nothing was committed.
